label: Eligibility
blurb: Who may sit NEET (UG) 2026 and who may actually be admitted to MBBS/BDS: age, qualifying examination and subjects, the marks and percentile bars, and the rules for NRI, OCI and foreign-national candidates.
authority: National Testing Agency — Information Bulletin, NEET (UG) 2026 (Chapters 6, 7 and 8)

blocks.heading: Age
blocks.intro: The bulletin applies the minimum-age rule notified in the Graduate Medical Education Regulations amendment of 16 June 2023.
items: You must have completed 17 years of age on or before 31 December of the year in which you sit the exam.

For NEET (UG) 2026 that means a date of birth on or before 31 December 2009. The bulletin sets the same lower age limit for General/UR, General-EWS, SC, ST, OBC-NCL and PwBD/PwD candidates alike — there is no relaxation by category.
There is no upper age limit. The bulletin records this citing NMC (UGMEB) letter no. U-11022/2/2022-UGMEB dated 9 March 2022.

blocks.heading: Qualifying examination and subjects
blocks.intro: The bulletin lists seven qualifying-examination codes (01 to 07). Codes 01 and 02 cover the overwhelming majority of Indian candidates.
items: The core requirement is Physics, Chemistry, Biology or Biotechnology, and English, with practical tests in the science subjects, at 10+2 or an equivalent level.

Code 01 — result awaited: if your Class 12 result has not been declared you may still apply and sit the test, but you will not be eligible for admission unless you have passed the qualifying examination by the time of the first round of counselling.

The additional-subject route is open. Candidates who took Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English as additional subjects after already passing Class 12, from a board recognised by the concerned government, may appear in NEET-UG and may be granted an Eligibility Certificate — the bulletin cites the NMC Public Notice dated 22 November 2023, decided in light of the flexibility the NEP allows in Class 12. Candidature is confirmed only on producing documentary evidence of the pass.

A degree route exists (Code 06): a B.Sc. of an Indian university with at least two of Physics, Chemistry, Biology (Botany, Zoology)/Biotechnology, provided you had earlier passed 10+2 with Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English.

If an Indian or foreign university examination is being claimed as equivalent to Class 12, an equivalence certificate from the concerned Indian University or the Association of Indian Universities is required. Candidates from foreign or international boards should check their qualification against Code 07.

blocks.heading: Minimum marks in the qualifying examination
blocks.intro: Separate from, and additional to, the NEET percentile bar. The condition below is the NTA eligibility rule as reproduced in MCC's UG counselling bulletin (https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s3e0f7a4d0ef9b84b83b693bbf3feb8e6e/uploads/2025/07/202509181307981517.pdf) for the immediately preceding cycle.
items: You must have passed Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English individually at the qualifying examination.
Unreserved and General-EWS: at least 50% marks in Physics, Chemistry and Biology/Biotechnology taken together.
SC, ST and OBC (Non-Creamy Layer): 40% instead of 50%.
PwBD: 40% instead of 50%, as per NMC and DCI regulations.
blocks.note: MCC re-issues its bulletin every cycle. Re-check this wording in the MCC NEET-UG 2026 bulletin once it is published.

blocks.heading: Qualifying percentile in NEET (UG) 2026
blocks.intro: The percentile is calculated against the highest marks in the All India common merit list, so the cut-off in marks moves every year. Only the percentile is fixed.
items: General / UR and General-EWS: 50th percentile.
SC, ST and OBC: 40th percentile.
PwBD candidates in the Unreserved and General-EWS categories: 45th percentile.
PwBD candidates in the SC, ST and OBC-NCL categories: 40th percentile.

If too few candidates in a category clear the bar in a given year, the Central Government — in consultation with NMC, DCI and the other regulators — may lower the minimum marks. Any such reduction applies to that academic year only.

blocks.heading: NRI, OCI and foreign nationals
items: NRIs, OCI cardholders and foreign nationals are eligible for admission to medical and dental colleges, but subject to the rules of the respective State Government, the institution and the Government of India — qualifying NEET alone creates no entitlement.
NRI and OCI candidates must upload a certificate from the Indian diplomatic mission in their country of residence along with the NEET application, and keep the original for counselling and admission.
A foreign national must upload documentary proof of citizenship — the relevant pages of a valid passport, or a certificate from the competent authority of the country of nationality.
OCI cardholders are entitled to the rights and privileges they held before the notification of 4 March 2021, in compliance with the Supreme Court order dated 3 February 2023 in W.P. No. 891 of 2021.
Indian citizens and OCI cardholders who intend to study medicine abroad must also qualify NEET (UG).
MCC's counselling for Deemed Universities covers 100% of their seats, including the 15% NRI quota.

blocks.heading: Reservation (All India Quota and central institutions)
blocks.intro: Applies to the 15% AIQ and to the AIIMS, JIPMER, ESIC and central university (DU, BHU, AMU) seats counselled by MCC.
items: SC 15%; ST 7.5%; OBC-NCL 27%; General-EWS 10%; PwBD 5% as horizontal reservation across each of the GEN, GEN-EWS, OBC-NCL, SC and ST pools.

OBC-NCL counts only if your community is on the current central list at ncbc.nic.in. A community on a state OBC list but not on the central list cannot claim OBC reservation here, and creamy-layer candidates are treated as Unreserved.
For seats filled by state authorities, the reservation policy of that state applies instead — not this table.

At counselling a PwBD candidate must produce a valid UDID card and the self-certified affidavits prescribed under the interim guidelines dated 19 July 2025, and appear before the designated medical board for verification.

label: Application
blurb: The two applications that matter — the NTA exam form and the MCC counselling registration — and the money behind them: exam fee, non-refundable registration fee, refundable security deposit, choice filling and locking.
authority: MCC — Information Bulletin & Counselling Scheme, NEET-UG (MBBS/BDS/B.Sc. Nursing) Counselling; NTA — Information Bulletin, NEET (UG) 2026

blocks.heading: Step 1 — the NEET (UG) 2026 exam form (NTA)
blocks.intro: Dates and fees below are from the NEET (UG) 2026 Information Bulletin (https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s37bc1ec1d9c3426357e69acd5bf320061/uploads/2026/02/20260208939209382.pdf).
items: Application window: 8 February 2026 to 8 March 2026, up to 9:00 PM.
Last date for a successful fee transaction by card, net banking or UPI: 8 March 2026, up to 11:50 PM.
Correction window: 10 March 2026 to 12 March 2026, and only in the fields NTA permits.
Examination: 3 May 2026 (Sunday), 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM IST — 180 minutes, 180 questions, 720 marks.
Fee: ₹1,700 General; ₹1,600 General-EWS / OBC-NCL; ₹1,000 SC / ST / PwBD / PwD / Third Gender; ₹9,500 for centres outside India. Gateway charges and GST are extra.

Your form is submitted only when the Confirmation Page is generated — money leaving your bank account is not proof of payment. The exam fee is never refunded and is not carried forward to a future exam.

blocks.heading: Step 2 — MCC counselling registration
blocks.intro: Qualifying NEET does not register you for counselling. After the result you register separately on mcc.nic.in for the seats MCC controls.
items: MCC counsels: the 15% All India Quota MBBS/BDS seats of the states; 100% of Deemed University seats (including their 15% NRI quota); AIIMS; JIPMER; central universities (DU, BHU, AMU, Jamia Millia Islamia); ESIC including the Insured Persons quota; and selected central B.Sc. Nursing institutes. For AFMC, MCC only does the registration and forwards the data — AFMC itself runs the selection.
The 85% state quota is not part of this. That is a separate registration on your state authority's portal.
One candidate, one registration form. MCC's scheme states that anyone found to have submitted more than one registration form is debarred from the allotment process and their candidature cancelled.

Your personal data is carried over from the NTA record. MCC will not edit your name, date of birth, category, caste or contact details at any stage — mistakes must be fixed on the NTA form, not later.

There is a one-time reset option at the registration page if you selected the wrong quota (for example Deemed when you wanted AIQ), but using it means registering again and paying the full fees again.

blocks.heading: The money at MCC registration
blocks.intro: Two separate payments: a non-refundable registration fee and a refundable security deposit.
items: AIQ / central universities / AFMC / ESIC / AIIMS / JIPMER / B.Sc. Nursing — registration fee ₹1,000 (UR/EWS) or ₹500 (SC/ST/OBC/PwD); security deposit ₹10,000 (UR/EWS) or ₹5,000 (SC/ST/OBC/PwD). A UR candidate therefore pays ₹11,000 in all; a reserved-category candidate ₹5,500.
Deemed Universities — registration fee ₹5,000, the same for every category; security deposit ₹2,00,000.
Registering for both government and Deemed seats does not mean paying twice: you pay only the higher set, i.e. the Deemed one — ₹5,000 plus ₹2,00,000.

The security deposit is refunded only after all rounds of counselling are complete and MCC notifies completion on its portal; the financial custodian then begins refunds within 15 days and completes them within 30 days of that notification.

The refund returns only to the exact card or bank account the payment came from, so keep that account open until it lands. MCC will not redirect a refund to another account, cannot refund to an NRI account under RBI rules, and pays no interest on the deposit.

blocks.heading: Choice filling and locking
items: Every round has its own fresh choice filling. The choices you filled for the previous round are treated as null and void — nothing carries forward.
Once locked, choices cannot be modified, changed or unlocked — not even by MCC, and not even if you locked a mistake.

If you are eligible for a round but do not submit fresh choices during its choice-filling window, you will not be considered for allotment in that round and will simply keep the seat you have already joined, if any.
blocks.note: As of mid-July 2026 MCC had not published the NEET-UG 2026 counselling schedule or bulletin — its latest UG notices still concerned security-deposit refunds for the 2025 cycle. Treat the fees and flow above as the standing scheme and confirm every date against the 2026 notification on mcc.nic.in when it appears.

label: Domicile
blurb: The 15% All India Quota is domicile-free; the 85% state quota is not. Each state writes its own definition of who belongs to it — and those definitions do not agree with one another.
authority: MCC counselling scheme; NTA Information Bulletin NEET (UG) 2026, Chapter 7; state counselling authorities (KEA, WB DME)

blocks.heading: The 15 / 85 split
items: In a state government medical or dental college, 15% of the seats go to the All India Quota, counselled by MCC. MCC's scheme states plainly that counselling for the 15% AIQ is domicile-free — where you live is irrelevant to it.

The other 85% is the state quota, counselled by the state's own authority. Under the NEET bulletin, admission to those seats is subject to the eligibility criteria and reservation policy prevailing in that State or UT, as notified by it from time to time.
The consequence: your NEET rank is national, but your access to the 85% is decided by a state-written eligibility clause that neither NTA nor MCC controls.

Some central institutions counselled by MCC also carry internal or domicile quotas of their own — JIPMER, and the 85% internal quota seats of DU and IP University, for example. MCC does not set those conditions; the institution does. MCC's own advice is to confirm your eligibility or domicile status for institutional-quota seats before you register and fill those choices.

blocks.heading: Every state defines it differently
blocks.intro: Two real examples, taken from the states' own counselling documents, show how far apart the tests sit.
items: Karnataka (KEA, UGNEET-2025 guidelines — https://cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/keawebentry456/ugneet2025/ugneet_Guidelineskannada.pdf): the main route, Clause (a), is a study test rather than a residence test — you must have studied and passed in government or government-recognised institutions in Karnataka for at least SEVEN academic years between Class 1 and Class 12, and have passed either SSLC/10th or 2nd PUC/12th from Karnataka. Clause (b) accepts 11th and 12th in Karnataka provided one parent studied in Karnataka for at least seven years. A separate route exists for candidates whose mother tongue is Kannada, Tulu, Kodava or Beary and who live outside the state — but it requires clearing KEA's Kannada language test.

West Bengal (Directorate of Medical Education, NEET UG 2025 counselling notice dated 31 July 2025 — https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s3aae8d1e00b15a30e5901227e97ffbef7/uploads/2025/07/2025073198.pdf): a residence test. Proforma A1 needs continuous residence in West Bengal for at least the last 10 years; Proforma A2 covers candidates who passed 10+2 from West Bengal in the current year with the same residence history; Proforma B covers candidates whose parents are permanent residents of West Bengal even where the candidate studied outside the state.
The same candidate, on the same facts, can therefore clear one state's test and fail another's.

blocks.heading: The traps
items: Studied-in-state, lived-in-state and parent-domicile are three different tests. Karnataka's main clause asks where you studied and for how long; West Bengal's asks where you have lived for ten years; a parent's residence or schooling can be the deciding fact in either.

A domicile or residence certificate on its own is frequently not enough. States demand the specific proof their clause names — a school study certificate countersigned by the education officer, a certificate in the state's own proforma, a parent's study certificate.

Failing the domicile test does not always shut you out of the state completely: in West Bengal, candidates who are not domiciled and are not taking the NRI route remain eligible for management-quota seats in private colleges — but not for the 85% state quota.
The 15% AIQ is the one route that asks none of this. If your state-quota claim is weak, that route is still fully open to you.
blocks.note: Never act on a summary — including this one — for a state-quota claim. Open the current-year information bulletin of the state authority you are claiming under, and read its eligibility clause and document list yourself.

label: Counselling
blurb: Round 1, Round 2, Round 3 (the old mop-up) and the stray vacancy round — where you can walk away for free, where it costs you your deposit, and where you are locked in for good.
authority: MCC — Information Bulletin & Counselling Scheme, NEET-UG (MBBS/BDS/B.Sc. Nursing) Counselling

blocks.heading: The rounds
blocks.intro: MCC's scheme records that the Supreme Court, by order dated 16 December 2021 in Nihila P.P. v. MCC, approved four online rounds of AIQ counselling.
items: Round 1 — registration, fees, choice filling, locking, allotment, physical reporting with original documents.
Round 2 — fresh registration for newcomers and fresh choices for everyone; no seats revert to the states after this round.
Round 3 — this is the old Mop-Up round, renamed. Upgradation is permitted up to this round.
Stray Vacancy Round — fresh registration and fresh choice filling; the last chance at an MCC seat.

blocks.heading: Round 1 — the free exit
items: Allotted a Round 1 seat and you simply do not report: you exit free. No forfeiture, and you continue into Round 2.

To KEEP the Round 1 seat while still trying to improve on it, you must physically report at the allotted college with your original documents and record a willingness to upgrade at the time of admission. Nobody may report on your behalf.
If you registered for Round 1 and were not allotted anything, you do not register again — you go straight to Round 2 choice filling.
If you are upgraded in Round 2 you must take relieving from the Round 1 college and join the Round 2 college; you retain no claim on the Round 1 seat.

blocks.heading: Round 2 — the deposit starts to bite
items: Allotted a Round 2 seat and you do not join it: your security deposit is forfeited.
You may still enter Round 3 afterwards — but only with a fresh registration and full payment of the fees again.

You may join the Round 2 seat and still upgrade: give the willingness to upgrade at the time of Round 2 reporting, and if you are upgraded in Round 3, vacate the Round 2 seat and join the new one. Candidates upgraded in Round 3 have no claim on the Round 2 seat.

blocks.heading: Round 3 — the point of no return
items: Once you JOIN a Round 3 seat you cannot resign it, surrender it or upgrade out of it. MCC's own scheme tells candidates to take a calculated decision before continuing into Round 3.
Allotted a Round 3 seat and you do not report: you exit with forfeiture of the security deposit and are eliminated from all further rounds, the stray round included.
Joining a Round 3 AIQ seat also bars you from participating in any counselling after it.

blocks.heading: Stray vacancy round
items: Fresh registration and fresh choice filling are required; nothing carries over from earlier rounds.
You are NOT eligible for the stray round if you did not register for it, if you are already holding or have joined a seat, or if you were allotted a Round 3 MCC seat and did not report.

MCC shares allotment data with the states after Round 3: if your name appears on a state's allotted list you are removed from the All India stray vacancy round. You cannot sit on a state seat and chase an AIQ stray seat at the same time.
Allotted a stray-round seat and you do not join: the security deposit is forfeited and you are out of any further rounds. Once you join, you cannot resign.

blocks.heading: Forfeiture — the short version
items: Round 1, not reported — free exit, deposit safe.
Round 2, allotted but not joined — deposit forfeited; Round 3 only on fresh payment.
Round 3, allotted but not reported — deposit forfeited and eliminated from further rounds.
Round 3, joined — no resignation, no upgrade, no further counselling.
Stray round, allotted but not joined — deposit forfeited, no further rounds.
Incorrect information about your eligibility, found at any stage — candidature cancelled for the remaining rounds and security deposit forfeited.
blocks.note: Four rounds are the scheme's baseline, but MCC has added rounds by notice in past cycles — in the 2025 cycle it ran a further round for BDS and B.Sc. Nursing seats and a special stray round (see the notices at https://mcc.nic.in/ug-medical-counselling/). The NEET-UG 2026 counselling schedule had not been published as of mid-July 2026; watch mcc.nic.in for it.
